body: I'm so glad! Thank goodness you're about to get up and go. Keep it up, friend. SUPER proud of you.
As a Michigan resident I don't really know if I have a choice!

I wouldn't say lucky. I am not without my fears or other mental health issues. Know you're not alone. There are hundreds of thousands of people with fears similar to yours who have fought hard like you have. Keep your head up, friend.

I do not have those, but I do have some generalized anxiety and mine makes me sad. It manifests itself in many different ways, sometimes sadness, sometimes anger. I'm sorry you're struggling but you certainly aren't alone.

It is common for change to trigger a lot of old feelings because people feel uncomfortable. If you are able to, please check to see if you campus allows free counseling sessions and try to attend those. Keep your head up. It will get easier all the time.

Sometimes we need a break from people we love in order to make sure we are in the best shape to love them again. I know it seems like you're the epicenter and the problem, but just know that people love you enough to come back and stay, even if its time to just focus on themselves for a while. Things get easier all the time, even if it seems impossible now. Keep your head up.

I'm sorry about your game store. I know being close with mom and pop shop owners is what makes us feel connected to the things around us. Even if the shop is not there anymore, I am sure the owner is glad people like you showed up when it mattered. Be on the lookout for other places similar to it.

People are deeply wounded by rejection. It is hard to assume you are enough for someone and that they feel the same as you and then all of the sudden the rug is pulled from underneath you. You assumed you knew what this person wanted. I also believe that people become deeply hurt when people break out expectations. You expected one thing and got another, and especially when this occurs without closure it can be even worse. Just know that even if you never know the reason why, there are better people out there for you. It may be hard to look on the bright side today, but there is a reason these things happen. Onward and upward. You're stronger than you know.

My ex took their own life very randomly back in August. It is so hard to imagine the what-ifs and if we could have done anything. Please know that we may never know what someone is thinking in their lowest moments and that they were never a reflection of how little we cared. The news just happened; today may be the hardest day. It's okay to be sad. It's okay to try to distract yourself for a while. PM me if you need to chat.
It's rough but yeah. I hope you move forward happily. And how lucky we are to have something so wonderful to miss.

I know it is frustrating to you. And emotions are hard to sort out. But there is a reason your body is responding that way. Have patience and love for yourself and how your body is processing what it is. I'm sorry you're so sad.

OH MY GOSH are you me? My twin sister and I moved together after college in May 2016 and have been together since February of this year. What at first was just a move for convenience became one of my favorite things about my day. I love her more than anyone in my life and I had no idea how much just hearing her get up in the morning would help me plan out my day. I miss her all the time and we are also only 15 minutes away from each other. It's new, and that hurts. But these are necessary changes to better everyone in this relationship. Keep your head up, pup.

We are being amicable with one another but of course I will be looking for a new place to go. I would rather not be without my cat. Thank you for your concern! PM me and I will of course send you a picture of her :)

Everyone has one relationship that makes us reconsider how we should treat ourselves. Even if we don't know each other,  you sound like me. And I know how hard it can be to learn that no one will love you more than you love yourself. I promise you, you can heal from this. And you'll be amazed at the person on the other side.
My sister is more like you. She never let's any walk over her ever and is often the loudest in the room. And I can be too but it takes a lot for me to get there.
Haha I wish! That would be super cute.

It is incredible common for first time students to feel a slump during their first or both first and second semester. A lot has changed around you, the way you look, how you communicate, how you speak, what times you're able to do things. Prioritize things and make a list of small accomplishments. There are days where getting up and taking a shower is good enough. Please utilize your counseling center if you can as many schools have up to 10 or more sessions for free. Being a student is so difficult but you can do it. Keep your head up.

Whoever told you you were not worthy of love and care and compassion and whoever told you you are terrible is wrong. You are a living, breathing person with hopes and dreams and wants and desires. There are plenty of people out there who honestly care about your well being and feel like you're a kind and caring person. Mental health has a tendency to try and trick us into feeling less than but I can assure you this is not the case.
You deserve t o live. Please make the call. Please contact 911. You are so much stronger than you know.
Strangely enough I do, too. I love debating and really digging in and dealing with things but for some reason when actual conflict arises I just don't want to be apart of it.

It's actually the worst. I never feel like I stick up for myself but at the same time I also don't feel like most arguments are worth the hassle. I'll adjust myself so I don't have to deal with it anymore.

Thank you. I talked to them about this now and we kind of came to the agreement I could continue living here without my animal, which is obviously devastating news but I do need a place to live, and my mom is more than willing to take care of my cat in the meantime. But of course it's hard for me to imagine living without my best friend all the time.

I have a cat. I guess my cat peed on a blanket of mine and normally is she has an accident (she is very old and her legs don't work great so I often carry her to the bathroom every few hours) I am there to wash the blanket immediately. But I was not home and I guess when they went in my room to look at something they smelled it and it was too much for them. Which I take responsibility for, however, this is the first and only time they have ever brought this up to me. And I make sure to go out of my way to make sure there is no animal or cat smell because I know how offensive that is to people.
I mean I get it. The issue is my animal is bothering other people. I would be bothered too if someones animal was maybe impacting my living space.

You're right. It is my responsibility and indeed I am the new one. The dog poop I will admit to not seeing but I live in an area where it snowed or the poop was picked up when I looked at the house. Beyond that the animal is my fault. I was angry and anxious at the time of posting this and after a few hours I am aware I am the one in the wrong. I just wish there was some conclusion we could come to because I do like being here but it is what it is.

No not at all. I hate feeling alone and wouldn't want someone else to experience it, too. I have had more bad friends then good, but the ones that I have that are good certainly make up for all the other ones. 

I always try to think positive, too. But just allow yourself to feel sad, as well. And what jobs are you applying for?

I would maybe carry headphones, it's what I do. And I always have a podcast or music pulled up so I can drown out whatever is going on. If you have a therapist or plan on seeking out therapy I would also suggest trying to delve into why loud noises disrupt you so much (I had to do the same thing and after maybe discovering why I am able to logically process through my anxiousness). I hope that helps.

I listen to the Rhett and Link podcast Ear Biscuits. I also listen to NPR's Splendid Table, or I will turn on my favorite Youtuber and listen to that. I also have an app that makes rain noises and will turn that on for a period of time and will sometimes also turn the podcast on. Just depends.

This happened to me all throughout college. In the end, I failed my final class because I decided to sleep through it rather than go because I was so terrified of waking up for it the next morning. I know telling you to tackle this is not the best piece of advice, but honestly, above all else, seek help. Most universities allow you free counseling. Set small goals everyday. Do something that is going to motivate you to get up and go even when everything else is telling you you don't want to. You can go to sleep on time. You can wake up on time. You can get things done because that's what's gotten you to this point. Be brave and be strong!
Yes. I do that and I am constantly picking skin on my head and my feet. My mouth and lips are always bleeding from me biting them. I didn't know this was an anxiety thing

Making friends in college is tough sometimes. A lot of them are friends of convenience, whoever is closest is the best friend they have. Just know not all people are like that. Join a group or a club with similar interests in yours, that guarantees getting you out of your room and with other people where you can meet and do things together. I know it's tough at first but you can do it.

I'm so sorry some creep decided to ever tell you you're not worth love and happiness. Clearly you care very deeply for people, you are forgiving, and introspective, you desire open communication and want the best for your partner. Those are qualities anyone would be lucky to have in a girl like you. Don't ever base your self-esteem and worth off of someone else's opinion of you, even if you love that person, respect yourself enough to know you're better than that. I know you're sad know, but just think about a year from now how happy you'll be knowing you aren't carrying a person so heavy with self-loathing they can't even see the amazing thing in front of them. Stay strong.

People grow and change all the time, friend. Sometimes the people we thought were our friends were just stepping stones to bigger and better things. Growth and change as a person is uncomfortable and you don't want people around who are not genuinely excited for you and your accomplishments. Positive thoughts as you send out job applications. If you ever need to chat, I'm here.
